result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0 at 102.171 s and stayed there; motor output followed and the aircraft lost altitude.
result.explanation: A control fault occurred on the propulsion loop: throttle went to 0 at 102.171 s with no recorded mode change. Motor output ch2 followed at once. The recording does not show who or what commanded zero.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=102.171 s to the end of the recording (14.254 s, 39 samples)
evidence.shows: Throttle was varying normally (53% at 101.784 s), then dropped to 0 and never recovered.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=102.69 s to the end of the recording (13.638 s, 44 samples)
evidence.shows: The motor channel went to its minimum value and froze shortly after the throttle command.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.993 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch2 is the throttle loop output. Over 60-116 s the correlation is 0.991 at lag 0, so the output stage obeyed the command.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=104.828 s: median 50.204 before, 31.72 after m
evidence.shows: Altitude fell from about 50 m to 18.369 m by the end, consistent with loss of thrust. This is an effect.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.392 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: The only 2 events are at start-up (Low voltage warning and a Sensor helth error). No mode change or failsafe is logged at the throttle drop.

checked.check: events: any mode change or failsafe near the throttle drop
checked.result: Only 2 events, both at t=0.392 s. None during the flight after start-up.

checked.check: sequence 85-110 s: earliest signal to leave baseline in the propulsion loop
checked.result: Throttle left baseline at 102.171 s, ch2 at 102.69 s, then pitch setpoint at 103.747 s, ch1 at 106.18 s and altitude at 106.278 s. Roll and yaw moved earlier, at 87.933-90.25 s.

checked.check: window 84-116 s: is the sheet SHIFT on throttle at 87.369 s real?
checked.result: No. Throttle varied up to 70% until the sample at 101.784 s (53%). The sheet SHIFT lines at 87.369 s (throttle) and 89.344 s (ch2) come from the final median. The real onset is 102.171 s.
Correlation 0.991 at lag 0 s. The output followed the command.
checked.about: Motor / ESC output stage (observed only as a commanded output value)

checked.check: compare at 102.2 s: what changed at onset
checked.result: Throttle and ch2 froze (throttle 38 -> 0 %, ch2 1404 -> 1100 us). Pitch tracking error rose 1.365 -> 3.076 deg (ratio 2.25). Roll and yaw tracking were about unchanged (ratios 1.23 and 1.08).
checked.about: Attitude loop is an effect, not the cause

checked.check: compare at 87.4 s: is the roll/yaw excursion a fault?
checked.result: Roll setpoint median rose 8.26 -> 34.17 deg and attitude followed (tracking ratio 1.35). This is a manoeuvre, not a fault.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=104.828 s: median 50.204 before, 31.72 after m
effects.why: Altitude loss follows the thrust loss.

effects.quote: SHIFT control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] changed level for good at t=106.889 s: median -2 before, 16.645 after deg
effects.why: The controller changed the pitch setpoint after thrust was lost (order from the sequence result).

effects.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good at t=106.506 s: median 1501 before, 1348 after us
effects.why: The pitch-loop output (ch1) followed the changed pitch setpoint; it reached 1100 by the end.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a11 t=105.841 s: vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] worse for good (typical |error| 1.388 -> 10.283) (see line 75; strength 3.171)
effects.why: Pitch tracking got worse after the throttle loss.

next_action.action: Extract mode, failsafe, RC throttle and battery data from the autopilot's own log.
next_action.why: Separates a pilot or RC cut, an autopilot failsafe, and a power-driven cut. This recording has no such signals.
how: Offline, from the flight controller's stored log (not a vehicle test), extract mode, failsafe flags and RC throttle input around the drop.
Extract battery voltage and current for the same window, plus the throttle-command source.
Check whether airspeed was 0 in that log too (a dead pitot vs a recording gap).
next_action.baseline: Same signals earlier in this flight, when throttle and ch2 tracked each other normally.

outcomes.label: RC throttle also went to 0
outcomes.means: The zero throttle came from the pilot or the RC link, upstream of the autopilot.
outcomes.then: Check RC link-loss and pilot report.

outcomes.label: RC normal, autopilot commanded 0 with failsafe flag
outcomes.means: The autopilot cut thrust by itself. The failsafe trigger (battery, sensor health) is the next question.

outcomes.label: Battery voltage collapsed before the drop
outcomes.means: A power problem is the trigger or main cause.
outcomes.then: Analyse the pack and the current draw.

unknowns: Who or what commanded throttle to 0 at 102.171 s: the recording has no mode, RC or failsafe signal there.
Battery voltage during the flight: the recording has no battery series, only the start-up warning.
Whether airspeed was really 0 for the whole flight or the sensor was not logged.

already_answered.question: When did the control fault occur?
already_answered.answer: The throttle command dropped to 0 at 102.171 s and never recovered. ch2 held 1100 from 102.69 s.

already_answered.question: Where on the aircraft was the fault?
already_answered.answer: The propulsion (throttle) loop, motor channel ch2. The attitude channels carried on.

data_requests.what: Flight controller's full log with mode, failsafe, RC input and battery voltage for this flight
data_requests.window: 90-116 s of flight 46, plus a normal earlier flight
data_requests.conditions: Same airframe and battery type, ideally a normal flight for comparison
data_requests.why_needed: Decides whether the zero throttle came from the pilot or RC link, an autopilot failsafe, or a power problem.

unobservable.fact: Physical state of the motor, ESC and battery during the drop
unobservable.why_it_matters: The Motor / ESC and Battery hypotheses depend on it; the recording only holds commanded outputs.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Inspect the ESC and motor; read ESC telemetry and battery pack logs if present.

hypotheses.claim: Throttle command was set to 0 upstream of the actuator output by the pilot, an RC link loss, or autopilot logic.
hypotheses.because: Throttle hit 0 with no logged event, and ch2 followed at lag 0 (correlation 0.991).
hypotheses.observed_at: controller throttle command and ch2 output as recorded

hypotheses.claim: The ESC or motor channel failed, so ch2 stopped following the throttle.
hypotheses.because: ch2 followed the throttle at lag 0, so the command had already dropped. The physical motor and ESC are not observed.

hypotheses.claim: Low voltage or a power fault triggered the throttle cut.
hypotheses.because: A Low voltage warning appears at start-up, but no battery series exists to test it near the drop.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor-health failure (the start-up Sensor helth error, airspeed constant 0) led the autopilot to cut thrust.
hypotheses.because: The error is logged at start-up and airspeed is 0 throughout, but nothing links it to the drop.

hypotheses.claim: A roll, pitch or yaw control fault caused the drop.
hypotheses.because: Roll and yaw excursions at 87-90 s are tracked manoeuvres. Pitch tracking worsened only after the drop (ratio 2.25).

events.what: Throttle command to 0 and ch2 held at 1100 us
events.why: Earliest change in the propulsion loop, with no logged reason.

events.what: Start-up Low voltage warning and Sensor helth error
events.why: Possible triggers, but there is no link to the drop in this recording.

events.what: Airspeed and yaw rate constant 0 all recording
events.why: Dead or unrecorded sensors; relevance to the fault is unknown.

events.what: Altitude loss, pitch setpoint shift, ch1 drop, worse pitch tracking
events.why: Follow the thrust loss; they start after ch2 froze.

events.what: Sheet SHIFT at 87.369 s and 89.344 s on throttle and ch2
events.why: Artifact of the final median; throttle varied normally until the drop.

result.lesson: No earlier cases were available (lessons returned none).
result.reuse_when: Applies to fixed-wing or multirotor UAVs on a mavros/PX4-style stack whose throttle command goes to 0 with no logged mode or failsafe event and the motor channel follows it at lag 0.
